justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are met: R-01 via 'WebRTC Streaming Router', R-02 via 'FHIR Translation Adapter' and 'National E-Prescription Adapter', R-03 through 'AI Symptom Checker Orchestrator' and Proxy, and R-04 via 'Consent Enforcement Middleware/Proxy Containers' and the external consent provider.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Performance under constrained conditions is thoroughly addressed using adaptive bitrate streaming in 'WebRTC Streaming Router', edge buffering in 'Local Async Event Bus / Queue Containers', and local caching via 'Store-and-Forward Cache Agent'.
justifications.compatibility: Meets R-08 cleanly with dedicated components: 'US FHIR Translation Module' (HL7 FHIR) and 'EU National E-Prescription Module' (National APIs), alongside standard OIDC integration with 'External Identity and Consent Provider'.
justifications.usability: Accommodates rural users facing network degradation down to 300 kbit/s via the 'WebRTC Streaming Router' degraded mode. However, separate patient and clinician client applications/interfaces are not distinctly modeled.
justifications.reliability: Fault tolerance for unstable rural connectivity is robustly designed with 'Store-and-Forward Cache Agent', write-ahead durable queuing in 'Local Durable Storage Engine', and local message buffering via 'MQTT Message Broker'.
justifications.security: Excellently addressed: 'ExtAuthz Filter' enforces default-deny consent and purpose checking, 'Regional Audit and Compliance Logging Subsystem' tracks AI inference versions for EU MDR/HIPAA, and 'PII/PHI Stripping Filter' protects telemetry.
justifications.maintainability: Clear modular separation of concerns: regional adapters for US/EU standards are isolated, consent logic is decoupled into Envoy proxies, and secret management and telemetry are encapsulated into discrete sidecars.
justifications.portability: Explicitly targets the specified GCP regions (europe-west3, us-central1) using containerized services, though components couple moderately to proprietary services like GCP Secret Manager, Cloud KMS, and GCP Persistent Disks.

PERF-01.justification: The architecture provides WebRTC gateways and ingress routing, but lacks explicit horizontal autoscaling, TURN server clustering, and media server capacity planning required to reliably negotiate and sustain 5,000 concurrent video sessions.
elements: Video Streaming Gateway Containers with Local Storage/Caching Agents
sensitivity_points: TURN/STUN server network bandwidth and throughput capacity under concurrent streams
Signaling channel connection latency during session establishment spikes
tradeoffs: Maintaining persistent media gateway states versus container statelessness and elasticity

PERF-02.justification: A rate of 50,000 requests per hour is approximately 14 requests per second. Lightweight gRPC routing and an asynchronous audit logging buffer easily handle this load well within 3 seconds.
sensitivity_points: External AI Symptom Checker Service inference latency and response times
Non-blocking asynchronous flushing of audit log buffers
tradeoffs: Synchronous audit logging ensures MDR compliance but risks increasing end-to-end response times

AVAIL-01.justification: The design explicitly includes adaptive bitrate WebRTC streaming, store-and-forward cache agents, and local MQTT brokers backed by persistent storage to buffer data during network drops without losing consultation state or notes.
elements: Video Streaming Gateway Containers with Local Storage/Caching Agents
Local Async Event Bus / Queue Containers
sensitivity_points: Bitrate degradation threshold tuning to prevent connection teardowns below 300 kbit/s
Local storage capacity for write-ahead logging during prolonged drops
tradeoffs: Video and audio quality degradation accepted to maintain active consultation connectivity

AVAIL-02.justification: The system only defines one US region (us-central1). Because data residency strictly forbids moving US patient data to the EU (europe-west3), total failure of us-central1 leaves no alternative regional deployment to restore service within 1 hour.
sensitivity_points: Single point of regional failure within the US cloud footprint
Data sovereignty constraints prohibiting cross-region failover to EU
tradeoffs: Cost optimization of single-region US deployment versus high availability and disaster recovery

MOD-01.justification: The architecture cleanly isolates prescription integrations into dedicated containers and components. Adding a new EU national format only requires updates within the EU National E-Prescription Module, leaving core services unaffected.
elements: FHIR Translation Adapter Container (US) and National E-Prescription Adapter Container (EU)
sensitivity_points: Interface decoupling between the core prescription service and national adapters
Extensibility of the EU National E-Prescription adapter framework
tradeoffs: Custom point-to-point adapters increase maintenance overhead compared to a single standard

MOD-02.justification: The AI Inference & Audit Proxy captures model versions, inputs, and outputs to ensure traceability. However, mechanisms for dynamic model rollbacks or version routing in the external AI service are not fully specified.
sensitivity_points: Model version tagging consistency across external inference requests
Audit trail immutability for MDR compliance
tradeoffs: Decoupled external AI service reduces deployment coupling but obscures rollback orchestration

SEC-01.justification: The architecture enforces default-deny controls using Envoy ExtAuthz filters. Requests missing explicit consent tokens are blocked, metadata headers enforce regional residency, and attempts are routed to regional audit subsystems.
elements: Regional Audit and Compliance Logging Subsystem
sensitivity_points: Policy evaluation speed and accuracy in the ExtAuthz filter
Integrity of data residency and consent purpose metadata headers
tradeoffs: Fine-grained inline consent checks increase request overhead on cross-border data calls

SEC-02.justification: Consent middleware enforces real-time API access rejection upon withdrawal. However, the model lacks data pipeline components, batch job controls, or audit workflows to verify research data purging or export cessation within 24 hours.
elements: Regional Audit and Compliance Logging Subsystem
sensitivity_points: Propagation delay of consent revocation from external provider to proxy filters
Absence of secondary analytics and research data store purging mechanisms
tradeoffs: Synchronous policy lookups avoid stale permissions but depend on external provider uptime
